tests_added_or_updated: 155 new, freshly and independently authored tests added in tests/test_cltr_cutover_136u_notification_marker_receipt_binding_independent_verification.py (1 skip), covering Group 9 exclusion, exact Group 10 inventory, Section 46 prerequisites, all three field tables, Section 16 conditional resolution (independently re-derived), authority-role prohibition on all three schemas, Tier 2 extension boundary, null-vs-absent behavior, sibling independence and four dependency graphs, atomic-completeness detection, wrong-family substitution, secret-like value probes, and no-network/no-dispatch/no-marker/no-receipt/no-authority/no-execution probes. Does not import 136T's test helpers or fixtures. Bounded repair: two pre-existing test files (136N, 136R) had their forbidden_stems guard-test tuples fixed to derive from LATER_GROUP_RECORD_FILES instead of a separately hardcoded, desynchronized copy (BLOCKING-136U-1).
summary: Phase 136U independently re-derived CLTR-CUTOVER-EXECUTABLE-SCHEMAS-001 v1.0's Sec.9, Sec.16, Sec.31, Sec.32, Sec.33, and Sec.46 directly from the frozen contract text (not from 136T's own summary), attempting to falsify every material 136T claim. Confirmed Group 9's schema-less exclusion (Sec.46's own text assigns zero schema files); confirmed the exact Group 10 inventory (NotificationAuthorityBinding, MarkerAuthorityBinding, FinalizationReceiptAuthorityBinding, no extras); confirmed Group 10 prerequisites are Group 1 (manifest-declared) plus Group 2/PFN-001 (conceptual only, no manifest $ref) -- not the full 1-9 conceptual chain. Recomputed all 21 manifest file_digest values byte-for-byte against actual file bytes (zero mismatches); confirmed registry count (22, the +1 being manifest.schema.json itself, architecturally expected). Reconstructed and adversarially attacked all three field tables (Sec.31/32/33) field-by-field, including every conditional branch (notification delivery_state x3, marker duplicate_of, receipt finalized-state bundle). Independently re-derived (not merely restated) that Sec.16's explicit if/then governs over Sec.33's summary 'yes' column for the receipt schema's finalized-state bundle -- the same specific-table-over-summary-text resolution rule already established by 136N/136P precedent. Independently re-assessed and confirmed all six of 136T's disclosed NON-BLOCKING-136T-1 through -6 discrepancies and DEFERRED-136T-1 (staleness_check). Confirmed authority_role 'authoritative' is locally forbidden on all three schemas with no case-variant, is_authoritative-forcing, or _extensions-smuggling bypass. Confirmed Tier 2 _extensions boundary on all three schemas. Rebuilt four independent graphs ($ref/manifest dependency, record identity, record digest, sibling independence) from scratch: acyclic, no Group 10 sibling cycle, no forced creation ordering. Confirmed atomic-completeness detection at the manifest layer (a partial Group 10 manifest fails ManifestIntegrityError). Built a fresh wheel and sdist, installed into an isolated venv outside the repository checkout, and exercised offline validation (registry construction, manifest verification, valid/invalid records for all three families) with socket.socket/socket.create_connection monkeypatched to raise -- zero network calls. Confirmed no dispatch/marker-write/receipt-write/authority-resolver module exists anywhere outside schema_resources/, and no runtime code references any Group 10 family outside schema_resources/ (git grep, confirmed empty). Found and repaired one genuine, reproducible Blocking defect (BLOCKING-136U-1): tests/test_cltr_cutover_136n_authorization_and_candidate.py and tests/test_cltr_cutover_136r_recovery_schema.py each carried a separately hardcoded forbidden_stems guard-test tuple that 136T's own Group 10 migration updated in LATER_GROUP_RECORD_FILES but missed in this second, independent copy -- causing both guard tests to fail deterministically (not a parallel-execution race; confirmed single-threaded, reproduced every run, unmodified since 136T's own commit) against 136T's own final tree, directly contradicting 136T's own claimed 1609/1609 combined-suite baseline (independently recomputed: the identical module set yields 1607 passed/2 failed pre-repair). Repaired by deriving both forbidden_stems tuples from LATER_GROUP_RECORD_FILES directly, eliminating the desync class structurally; no production schema, manifest, or shared-definition file was touched. Combined Groups 1-10 + schema-runtime + 136U suite: 1764 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped post-repair (1762 passed, 2 failed, 1 skipped pre-repair). Fast Green: 4391/4391 passed, matching 136T's own count exactly. Full unmarked suite, fresh run on the clean committed post-repair tree: 21820 passed, 22 failed, 1 skipped -- zero of the 22 touch cltr_cutover/schema_runtime/manifest/packaging (grep-confirmed); 21 exactly match 136T's own previously-disclosed baseline categories; 1 additional node (test_risk_register.py::test_risk_register_no_repository_files_created) independently re-run in isolation and passed 1/1, the same pre-existing parallel-execution git-status race category (NON-BLOCKING-136Q-1/-136S-2/-136T-7), with the specific extra node ID observed varying run-to-run against live, uncommitted governed-lifecycle state -- itself further confirmation of the pre-existing category, not a new defect. Reviewed and re-confirmed all fourteen inherited findings (136M-1 through -4, 136N-7, 136P-1/2, 136Q-1, 136R-1 through -4, 136S-2, 136T-1 through -7, DEFERRED-136T-1) -- none converted to Blocking beyond the one repaired this phase, none amplified. Zero unresolved Blocking findings. Legacy lifecycle remains the sole production authority; CLTR remains derivative; runtime remains Observed / observe / execution unavailable. Verdict: VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- READY FOR NEXT EXECUTABLE-SCHEMA GROUP.
